To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) White females who have supportive peers reported being more adjusted to college; 2) Hispanic females who had supportive parents reported being better adjusted; and 3) self-esteem is an important predictor of college adjustment among all groups except for Hispanic males.
Self-Esteem, Parental Support, and Peer Support are Predictors of College Adjustment.

Self-esteem was predictive of overall adjustment to college among White females and males, and among Hispanic females; parental education level was predictive among White and Hispanic females; and peer support was predictive among White females.
